entry.title: Post-adiabatic effects sourced by radiation reaction for inspiraling, eccentric binaries in post-Newtonian theory
entry.summary: The adiabatic approximation, in which eccentric binaries evolve under orbit-averaged fluxes, is widely used in gravitational-wave and astrophysical modeling. We use resummed multiple-scale analysis, which is closely related to near-identity averaging transformations, to derive post-adiabatic corrections from leading-order radiation reaction and explain how the accuracy of the adiabatic approximation depends on the initial orbital phase. While the secular evolution equations for the eccentricity and semi-major axis receive no explicit first post-adiabatic corrections, their solutions acquire such corrections through the initial conditions. We also derive the change in the functional form of the gravitational-wave polarizations that cancels the gauge dependence of the orbital elements at first post-adiabatic order, ensuring agreement between waveforms evaluated at the same physical event in different coordinates. At a radial turning point, the first post-adiabatic oscillations of the semi-major axis and eccentricity vanish, so the initial osculating energy and angular momentum agree with their orbit-averaged values up to second post-adiabatic corrections. When initialized elsewhere along the orbit, the adiabatic approximation can accumulate significant dephasing, which the first post-adiabatic approximation can substantially reduce. Both dephasings can change sign across parameter space, consistent with competing contributions from successive orders. Accounting for initialization is therefore essential for assessing the accuracy of these approximations, particularly for long-lived, highly eccentric binaries.

entry.title: Conic Tilings of Black Hole Images by Radial Closest Approach
entry.summary: Each point in a black hole image corresponds to a light ray, whose minimum radial coordinate when traced backward from the observer measures how deeply it probes the spacetime. We show that contours of constant closest-approach radius form arcs of conic sections in standard Bardeen image coordinates for Kerr, and in natural local image coordinates for finite-radius observers in the broader Plebanski-Demianski (PD) family of Einstein-Maxwell solutions. At each radius, the condition of vanishing radial velocity defines a complete conic; the physical contour consists of those points whose rays reach that radius before encountering an outer turning point. For positive Killing energy and positive mass, we prove that throughout connected positive-radius regions with positive radial metric function and allowed motion at both endpoints, a local test of the radial potential's slope is sufficient to select the physical arcs. This simplification follows from a coefficient identity imposed by the PD field equations and alignment of the principal null directions. We give explicit counterexamples in a domain crossing r=0 and in the separable Ovcharenko-Podolsky extension, where an outer turning point invalidates the local test. The conic family also yields a single polynomial equation containing the critical curve in Kerr and PD. These results turn the returning image into a geometric map of radial photon propagation, independent of the emission model. (This abstract has been abridged to meet the arXiv character limit.)

entry.title: New Physics in Ultra-High-Energy Neutrino Flavor
entry.summary: Neutrino flavor measurements test physics beyond the Standard Model that modifies neutrino production, propagation, or detection. IceCube has measured the flavor composition of the astrophysical neutrino flux up to PeV energies. Next-generation experiments will extend flavor measurements to the ultra-high-energy (UHE) regime, $100\,\mathrm{PeV}$-$10\,\mathrm{EeV}$, by combining in-ice radio detection with Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. We present the first study of the new-physics reach of these projected UHE flavor measurements. We take Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) as a benchmark, since its effects grow as a power of the neutrino energy. We find that UHE flavor ratios will be the most sensitive probe of LIV for operators of dimension four and higher, improving on current bounds from all sectors by up to twenty orders of magnitude. Three-flavor observables improve this sensitivity by up to an order of magnitude over Earth-skimming tau neutrinos alone.

entry.title: Squeezed Light Generation by Cooper Pair Recombination in a Superconductor-Semiconductor Structure
entry.summary: We theoretically demonstrate squeezed light generation in a compact, electrically driven device utilizing the nonlinear light-matter interaction of Cooper-pair recombination in a hybrid superconductorsemiconductor structure. On the basis of second-order perturbation theory, we developed an effective Hamiltonian which incorporates the electronic component of the interaction as a photon coupling strength coefficient, enabling a model to describe the quadrature squeezing effect of Cooper-pair recombination on the photonic state. We find the squeezing strength to be proportional to the superconducting energy gap squared and device length, as well as increasing with applied voltage. For practical device length, materials and voltage bias, we calculated squeezing values comparable to those of existing squeezed light generation methods when operating below the critical temperature. This theoretically developed concept shows viability for electrically pumped squeezed light generation and can pave the way towards realization of squeezing in compact integrated structures.

entry.title: Symmetry-Enabled Rolling of Composite Bosons: A Route to Superconductivity from Strong Repulsion with $T_c$ Proportional to the Electron Bandwidth
entry.summary: Motivated by superconductors discovered in systems with a strong Coulomb repulsion, we ask whether such a repulsion can give rise to superconductivity with a transition temperature $T_c$ bounded only by the electron bandwidth. Coulomb repulsion can produce pairing as it binds electrons to holes. If each hole binds three electrons into a three-electron-one-hole (3e1h) composite, the condensation of these bosonic composites can give rise to superconductivity. However, the resulting $T_c$ falls far below the electron bandwidth in the controlled regime where the binding is much stronger than the carriers' kinetic energy. This is because, on a lattice, a tightly bound composite usually has to move through a higher-order process where the intermediate state costs an energy of order the binding energy, so that the strong binding makes the composite heavy, limiting the superfluid stiffness and hence $T_c$. Here, we show that symmetry offers a way around this tradeoff. In lattices satisfying certain symmetry requirements, a composite can move by single-particle hops without any costly intermediate state, a motion we call rolling. Such rolling keeps the mass of the composite finite even for an infinitely strong binding, so that a $T_c$ proportional to the electron bandwidth can be achieved in the controlled regime. We derive a criterion for rolling and apply it to construct all fourteen minimal lattice models that support such rolling. We show that rollable 3e1h composites can indeed be stabilized in the ground state. We then propose to realize such superconductivity in a dual-gate bilayer, and use exact numerics to show that $T_c$ can reach a few percent of the electron hopping. These results establish rollability as a guiding principle in the search for and design of superconductors in strongly repelling electron systems, with the minimal models constructed here as prototypes.

entry.title: Probing Krylov Dynamics in Driven Many-Body Systems
entry.summary: Krylov complexity has become a central probe of operator growth, scrambling, and quantum chaos. Yet, a basic fact hinders its experimental study: laboratory quantum systems are routinely driven in time, whereas the Krylov construction assumes a fixed generator and breaks down once the Hamiltonian varies. Here, we solve the time-dependent many-body Krylov problem exactly and in closed form for scale- and rotation-invariant systems realized in current quantum-simulation and control platforms. We find exact relations that map the driven dynamics onto mutually orthogonal Krylov subspaces and yield a closed-form spread complexity, determined solely by the spectral properties of the initial Hamiltonian and the driving schedule. The construction extends to Liouville space and solves the time-dependent density-matrix Krylov problem, which makes the Krylov dynamics of initial thermal states experimentally accessible. In scale-invariant quantum gases, such as the driven Lieb-Liniger model, the Tonks-Girardeau gas, and the Calogero-Sutherland model, the complexity is set by the width of the atomic cloud and its rate of change, directly accessible via in situ and time-of-flight imaging. In rotation-invariant spin systems such as the Haldane-Shastry and central-spin models, it is governed by collective spin precession that can be probed and read out in trapped-ion, cavity-QED, and circuit-QED platforms.

entry.title: ViViViT: a Video-to-Video Vision Transformer for Cosmological Lightcone Reconstruction
entry.summary: Moving along the line of sight of a cosmological lightcone also moves through cosmic time, as in a video of cosmic structure traced by an evolving observable. We recast the reconstruction of the underlying matter field from observed lightcones as a video-to-video translation task by introducing ViViViT, a vision transformer that factorizes attention across transverse frames and radial evolution. On reconstructed matter fields from 21cm neutral hydrogen simulations over $z\in[7.66,16.00]$, ViViViT preserves spectral power and phase alignment within a few percent of the ground truth up to the Nyquist scale, and three-point correlations for all triangle configurations with sides up to $k\simeq0.77\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$, outperforming a convolutional 3D-U-Net baseline across all measured statistics. By encoding the evolving geometry of the cosmological observable itself, ViViViT marks a step toward field-level architectures that natively respect cosmic time, opening the path to time-aware reconstruction of cosmic tracers and targeted searches for redshift-dependent signatures in 21cm data.

entry.title: The NANOGrav 15-year data set: A Limit on Continuous Spin Gravitons
entry.summary: Continuous spin particles (CSPs) are massless particles characterized by a dimensionful spin scale, $ρ$, which, when non-zero, changes their helicity under Lorentz boosts. Since CSPs reduce to ordinary particles when $ρ\rightarrow 0$, the photon or graviton could be CSPs and only appear to behave as ordinary particles due to a small value of $ρ$. Therefore, it is important to determine what value of $ρ$ is experimentally allowed. Recent work has shown that the physical effects of CSPs scale as powers of $ρ/ω$ when $ρ\ll ω$, where $ω$ is a frequency scale, making low-frequency probes particularly beneficial for highlighting these phenomena. In this paper we use pulsar timing arrays to set constraints on the spin scale of the continuous spin graviton. Pulsar timing arrays are uniquely suited for this application as they have exceptional sensitivity to low, nanohertz frequency gravitational waves, as demonstrated by their recent evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. Using standard Bayesian data analysis techniques, we find that the NANOGrav 15-year data set constrains the graviton spin scale to $ρ_\text{g} < 1.23 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{eV} $ at the 95% credible level.

entry.title: Type Ia-CSM Supernovae. I. Uniform Light-Curve Characterization and Inference on the Underlying Type Ia Explosions
entry.summary: We present the largest uniform study to date of 50 thermonuclear Type Ia supernovae interacting with circumstellar medium (SNe Ia-CSM). As the first paper in a series delineating the population properties of this class, this work focuses specifically on a uniform analysis of their light curves. Our results show that SNe Ia-CSM display a significantly more uniform light-curve morphology than interacting core-collapse SNe IIn, closely resembling the luminous-slow subgroup. The Ia-CSM sample spans approximately an order of magnitude in peak luminosity, total timescale, and radiated energy, with a median optical peak luminosity of $\approx2\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$ ($\approx-20$ mag). We find a distinct bimodality in the radiated energy distribution: a predominant population of energetic events with $\approx 2\times10^{50}$ erg and characteristic timescales of $\approx100$ days, and a secondary population that is roughly an order of magnitude less energetic with shorter timescales of $\approx50$ days. Decomposition of the luminosity contributions from underlying SN Ia and CSM interaction by the Ia-CSM spectral classification reveals a diverse range of underlying SN Ia subtypes spanning from luminous 1991T-like to faint 1991bg-like. Both SN Ia and CSM properties are broadly consistent with the core-degenerate channel resulting from common-envelope evolution followed by core merger, where the presence of dense CSM is dictated by the delay time between the common-envelope phase and the thermonuclear explosion. Subsequent papers in this series will utilize numerical simulations, semi-analytical modeling, spectroscopy, and host-galaxy environments to further constrain the progenitor and explosion pathways to SNe Ia-CSM.

entry.title: Robustness of the Baryonic Acoustic Oscillation Peak Position against Monopole Fluctuations in Galaxy Surveys
entry.summary: Precise measurements of the baryonic acoustic oscillation (BAO) peak position are one of the key goals in modern galaxy surveys. We investigate the impact of the monopole fluctuations in galaxy surveys on the BAO peak position in the galaxy two-point redshift-space multipole-correlation functions. The background mean density of a galaxy sample is estimated from the survey itself by averaging the observed galaxy number density, and this averaged number density (monopole) is subtracted to obtain the observed galaxy number density fluctuation, which includes an additional contribution from the monopole fluctuations, propagating to galaxy clustering analysis. We compute the contributions of the monopole fluctuations to the redshift-space multipole-correlation functions. While the monopole contributions in galaxy two-point correlation function are anisotropic and non-negligible in amplitude, the contributions are so smooth around the BAO peak position that they are almost completely absorbed in the BAO broadband model, leaving the BAO peak position unaffected at the sub-percent level. Our results demonstrate the robustness of the BAO analysis against the unknown systematic error.

entry.title: Early-Excess SNe Ia Show Strong C II Absorption
entry.summary: Some type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) exhibit an early excess in their rising light curves, but the physical origin of this behavior remains uncertain. The processes driving these excesses affect the ejecta at early times and may also imprint on the outermost layers. We investigate whether early excesses are associated with differences in unburned material by measuring pre-maximum carbon absorption. Using multi-component Gaussian fits to the blended Si II $\lambda6355$ and C II $\lambda6580$ region, we measure pseudo-equivalent widths and velocities for a sample of 35 nonpeculiar SNe Ia with rising light curve categorizations. We find that early-excess objects ($n=13$) tend to exhibit stronger C II absorption than non-excesses ($n=22$) at phases earlier than approximately $-13$ d, with a two-sample K-S test of the earliest measurements yielding $p=0.025$. In contrast, the HV Si II components do not clearly separate the two groups. Early-excess SNe Ia tend to be more luminous and decline more slowly, but objects with similar maximum-light properties span a range of C II pseudo-equivalent widths, suggesting that this effect is distinct from the known luminosity-width relation. We show that, at least in some cases, when objects have similar light-curve shape and photospheric temperature, the effect we see is not driven by ionization but by distinct differences in the explosion, such as carbon abundance and density and the efficiency of burning in the WD. Our results provide a new constraint on SN Ia explosion models for early excesses, as they must produce a tendency for stronger early C II absorption.

entry.title: When Nonlocal Total Derivatives Are Not Variationally Trivial
entry.summary: We study total time derivatives in infinite-order and nonlocal Lagrangian mechanics. In the formal infinite-order setting, such terms remain variationally trivial. For nonlocal functionals on trajectories, however, exactness in the form $L=DW$ is not sufficient to ensure a vanishing nonlocal Euler-Lagrange expression. We exhibit a smooth convolution-type counterexample.

entry.title: Spins do not add: why rotating stars do not help spin-up black holes in binaries
entry.summary: It is well-known that in the merger of a black-hole binary with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum, the spin of the final black hole always increases with the spin of the components. We show that this very intuitive behavior is violated in black hole--neutron star binaries, where the spin of the final black hole actually decreases as the spin of the neutron star increases. Using a large set of binaries with different spins and mass ratios, we identify the mechanism behind this surprising result in the nonlinear dynamics of the tidal disruption, which drives a substantial loss of angular momentum via dynamical ejecta, in some cases comparable to that radiated via gravitational waves. Our results highlight that the spin evolution of stellar-mass black holes involved in binary mergers is different from what normally assumed, far more complex, and interesting.

entry.title: Singlet-triplet superconductivity from repulsive interactions in a $p$-wave magnet
entry.summary: Motivated by recent proposals of $p$-wave magnets, which host odd-parity spin splitting, we study electrons near Van Hove singularities with local repulsive interactions. We demonstrate how the symmetry of the $p$-wave spin splitting governs the competition among instabilities. Using a parquet renormalization group (pRG) analysis of a simple one-sublattice model of a $p$-wave magnet, we find that superconductivity is the leading instability over the entire phase diagram for purely repulsive interactions. The resulting superconducting state is generically a mixture of spin-singlet and spin-triplet pairing and approaches an equal-weight mixture when $T_c$ is small compared with the energy offset between each Van Hove electron and its inversion partner. Extending the pRG analysis to a more realistic two-sublattice model, we find that superconductivity remains the leading instability, while the sublattice degree of freedom leads to a competition among various singlet-triplet pairing channels and even a finite-momentum equal-spin pair-density wave. Our mechanism applies broadly to odd-parity magnets and opens a natural route to nodal topological superconductivity.

entry.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
entry.summary: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using Lüscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI. Finally, we identify metastable resonances in the spectrum.

entry.title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
entry.summary: The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. For a $Γ$-law polytropic equation of state, these solutions, which we call singustars, are thick shells bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces around a naked, repulsive, negative-mass singularity, with a Schwarzschild exterior. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass $M$ and the compactness $C\equiv M/R$. Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with $Γ= 2$ are stable only for $M\lesssim0.63$ and $C\lesssim0.25$, a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.

entry.title: Spontaneous breaking of a continuous symmetry at a non-conformal quantum critical point in one dimension
entry.summary: In this work, we present numerical evidence for the spontaneous breaking of a continuous $U(1)$ symmetry in a nearest-neighbor interacting spin-1 chain at a quantum critical point separating two XY quasi-long-range ordered phases distinguished by a spontaneously broken $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry. Remarkably, the continuous symmetry breaking emerges precisely at the critical point of the discrete order parameter, suggesting a novel mechanism beyond currently established scenarios. At criticality, the XY correlations develop true long-range order, accompanied by a finite perpendicular magnetization, a zero-frequency Bragg peak in the transverse dynamical structure factor, and sharp gapless collective excitations. From complementary static and dynamical observables, we quantitatively determine the critical exponents, obtaining a dynamical exponent $z=1.50\pm0.04$ and an anomalous dimension $η=1.04\pm0.03$. We further show that the non-interacting continuum limit is equivalent to the recently introduced transverse quantum fluid, displaying their off-diagonal long-ranged order in one dimension. Complementing the numerical study, we derive the renormalization-group flow equations of the continuum theory to second order in the $\varepsilon$ expansion. We identify an interacting fixed point whose critical behavior differs from the Ising universality class already at two-loop order, although the perturbative exponents remain far from the numerical values.

entry.title: Conformal Holographic Dark Energy and the Neutrino-Mass Tension
entry.summary: Recent DESI results suggest a preference for evolving dark energy (DE) over a cosmological constant, motivating the exploration of alternative models for the background expansion. These data also lead to neutrino-mass constraints close to the lower bounds permitted by oscillation experiments. In this work, we propose and test a conformal holographic dark energy (CHDE) model in which the DE density depends on a power law of the conformal time, characterized by an exponent $n$. The model introduces one additional parameter relative to $Λ$CDM and reduces to it in the limit $n=0$. We confront CHDE with BAO, CMB, and SNe Ia datasets, following the combinations used by DESI, and perform parameter inference in both flat and non-flat cosmologies. We find a consistent preference for $n\simeq -0.25$ to $-0.32$, with uncertainties below $\pm 0.1$, and disfavor the $Λ$CDM limit at the $4.4$--$4.5σ$ level; however, the model-comparison statistics provide no consistent preference for CHDE over $Λ$CDM. The resulting neutrino-mass constraints remain compatible with terrestrial limits and yield posterior distributions that peak at positive values, avoiding the negative-mass preference found in $Λ$CDM. The CHDE model is therefore consistent with current observational constraints and provides a viable alternative to constant dark energy.

entry.title: Super $T\bar{T}$ deformation and the RNS non-critical superstring
entry.summary: In this paper we review the super $T\bar{T}$ deformation of $\mathcal{N}=(1,1)$ theories in the superspace formulation, alongside its interpretation in the context of noncritical string theory. By combining the superspace approach with concepts from the study of super-Riemann surfaces, we demonstrate that super $T\bar{T}$ deformations in superspace can be naturally interpreted as a noncritical RNS superstring theory. We also propose a possible interpretation of the super $T\bar{T}$ deformations as 2D supergravity in the superspace through some field redefinitions.

entry.title: Connecting field-level and n-point function measurements of galaxy bias
entry.summary: Precise measurements of galaxy bias parameters are essential for extracting cosmological information from galaxy surveys. Field-level analyses infer bias coefficients at a finite cutoff $Λ$, typically related to the lattice resolution, while $n$-point function analyses typically adopt renormalization conditions defined in the low-$k$ limit. In this work, we use the renormalization group (RG) to relate field-level measurements at different cutoffs and connect them to $n$-point function measurements. We generate mock galaxy fields with a Lagrangian perturbation theory forward model and a galaxy bias expansion, and then measure the bias parameters across a range of cutoffs. We show that the RG predictions describe the measured running and, in the limit $Λ\to 0$, agree with the (tree-level) $n$-point function measurements of first-order $b_δ$ and second-order $b_{δ^2}, b_{{G}_2}$. We also measure the running on halo catalogs based on full $N$-body simulations and show that the RG prediction describes the measurements well within the predicted systematic errors. Our results establish the RG flow as a natural formulation for relating galaxy bias measurements at different cutoffs and connecting the schemes used in field-level and $n$-point function analyses.

entry.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
entry.summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).

entry.title: Dimensional Crossover and Correlated Spin Dynamics in the Chain-Like van der Waals Antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$
entry.summary: We report a comprehensive investigation of the magnetic properties and spin dynamics of the chain-like van der Waals antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ using magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The magnetic susceptibility exhibits a broad maximum near 250 K, characteristic of strong short-range antiferromagnetic correlations in a low-dimensional system. A classical Fisher-chain analysis gives an effective intrachain exchange scale $J/k_B\approx 140$ K, while a quantum $S=3/2$ nearest-neighbor-chain calculation yields $J/k_B\approx 114$ K. A constrained AF-FM zig-zag-chain calculation is also compatible with the susceptibility, supporting a dominant quasi one dimensional antiferromagnetic exchange scale of order 100 K. $^{31}$P NMR measurements provide microscopic insight into both static and dynamic spin correlations. The $K-χ$ relation displays two distinct linear regimes separated near $T^\ast\approx 250$ K, with different slopes indicating a change in the effective transferred hyperfine couplings. Below $T_{N}$, the relaxation follows $1/T_1\propto T^5$, consistent with magnon-mediated relaxation in the ordered state. The temperature dependence of the internal hyperfine field yields a critical exponent $β\approx 0.36$, consistent with three-dimensional universality. Together, these results establish AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ as a quasi-one-dimensional $S=3/2$ antiferromagnet embedded in a layered van der Waals host, in which local probes directly resolve the crossover from correlated intrachain spin dynamics to anisotropic three-dimensional magnetic order. More broadly, AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ provides a useful van der Waals platform for studying dimensional crossover, correlated spin dynamics, and hyperfine-coupling evolution in low-dimensional antiferromagnets.

entry.title: Vacuum polarization and cyclotron resonance effects on radiative transfer and plasma deceleration in subcritical X-ray pulsars
entry.summary: We investigate the spectrum and polarization of radiation emerging from a subcritical X-ray pulsar using self-consistent radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of an accretion channel in a strong magnetic field. The polarized radiative transfer in the channel above the hot spot is simulated for the two normal modes, taking into account resonant Compton scattering in a strongly magnetized plasma and the effects of vacuum polarization. We show that the deceleration of the accreting matter in the subcritical regime is mainly governed by resonant scattering. Our simulations provide the velocity profiles of the plasma flow and demonstrate that vacuum polarization dominates over plasma birefringence, enhancing both the cyclotron spectral feature and the radiative deceleration of the plasma. We also find that the energy of the cyclotron feature increases with accretion luminosity, indicating a positive correlation consistent with previous observational results and theoretical interpretation.

entry.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (I): a $[3,-1]$ block and a non-Gorenstein toric phase
entry.summary: We construct and analyze a mirror family for the generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefold $X_+=[\mathbb{P}^1\,|\,3\ {-1};\ \mathbb{P}^4\,|\,2\ 3]$, with $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(2,46)$. We introduce auxiliary variables to obtain a toric GIT presentation with two chambers. The first gives $X_+$, while the second gives a Calabi-Yau threefold $X_-$ related to $X_+$ by a flop of 16 disjoint $(-1,-1)$-curves. The threefold $X_-$ is a nef complete intersection in a non-Gorenstein toric $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano eightfold. Then the Hori-Vafa equations give a 2-parameter Laurent family, and we construct a smooth projective crepant model $Y$ of its general member with mirrored Hodge numbers. The rank-6 Picard-Fuchs system of $Y$ has two maximally unipotent boundary points, whose indicial algebras are isomorphic to the even cohomology rings $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_+,\mathbb{C})$ and $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_-,\mathbb{C})$. We also show that the predicted genus-zero BPS numbers of the first two vertical degrees agree with direct counts of lines and conics on the genus-one fibration $X_-\to\mathbb{P}^2$.

entry.title: Superdilations at Schwarzschild null infinity and beyond
entry.summary: Relying on the definition of asymptotic conformal Killing horizons, the generators of asymptotic conformal symmetries at future null infinity in Schwarzschild space-time is computed. Supertranslations and superdilations are generated by two independent functions on the sphere, and the generators close an enlarged algebra with respect to the BMS one. For a generic asymptotically flat space-time, the superdilations Iyer-Wald charge is non-trivial but divergent at the boundaries of null infinity, where its growth rate is fixed by the asymptotic values of the Bondi mass aspect. Such a rate equals the monopole supertranslation charge, for which antipodal matching is well posed and trivially satisfied in the Schwarzschild geometry, where, furthermore, only the global dilation mode contributes. Its growth reflects the explicit time dependence of the generator rather than radiation. The effect of superdilations on a pair of celestial observers is an angle-dependent dilation rate, related to the local density of the charge.

entry.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
entry.summary: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.

entry.title: Validation of the DESI DR2 Ly$α$ BAO analysis using synthetic datasets
entry.summary: The second data release (DR2) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), containing data from the first three years of observations, doubles the number of Lyman-$α$ (Ly$α$) forest spectra in DR1 and it provides the largest dataset of its kind. To ensure a robust validation of the Baryonic Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) analysis using Ly$α$ forests, we have made significant updates compared to DR1 to both the mocks and the analysis framework used in the validation. In particular, we present CoLoRe-QL, a new set of Ly$α$ mocks that use a quasi-linear input power spectrum to incorporate the non-linear broadening of the BAO peak. We have also increased the number of realisations used in the validation to 400, compared to the 150 realisations used in DR1. Finally, we present a detailed study of the impact of quasar redshift errors on the BAO measurement, and we compare different strategies to mask Damped Lyman-$α$ Absorbers (DLAs) in our spectra. The BAO measurement from the Ly$α$ dataset of DESI DR2 is presented in a companion publication.

entry.title: Weyl Rescalings: A First Order Approach
entry.summary: Weyl transformations, --local rescalings in which the metric transforms as $g_{μν}(x)\longrightarrow Ω^2(x)\, g_{μν}(x)$--, are expected to be a symmetry of nature at extremely high energy, that should be (spontaneously) broken at low energy. In Cartan's first order formulation of gravity this translates into the condition that the local frames (vielbein) scale as $e^a(x) \longrightarrow Ω(x) e^a(x)$. In this construction, the Lorentz connection one-form fields $ω^a{}_b$ are independent from $e^a$, and since Lorentz transformations and dilatations commute, $ω$ and $R(ω)$ must be Weyl invariant, while in the second order metric formalism the Ricci tensor undergoes a non-homogeneous transformation. This generates a tension between the two formulations, which should be equivalent in the vanishing torsion limit. Here we show how the puzzle can be resolved taking into account the role of torsion. This also sheds some light on the conformal coupling of matter fields to gravity.

entry.title: The Higgs boson, naturalness, and the Universe
entry.summary: The Higgs boson -- the only known fundamental scalar particle -- may have profound implications for both particle physics and cosmology. This review examines how the Higgs field may have influenced the Universe from its earliest moments to its present state. We first discuss particle-physics puzzles, including the naturalness and hierarchy problems, as well as the possible metastability of the electroweak vacuum. We then turn to cosmological scenarios where the Higgs boson could be a driving force, including Higgs inflation, reheating and the onset of the hot Big Bang, the electroweak phase transition, and baryogenesis via electroweak processes.
entry.arxiv:comment: 38 pages, 4 figures. Invited topical review, published in Reports on Progress in Physics

entry.title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
entry.summary: We investigate inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of atomic and molecular line photons as an explanation of the evolving MeV spectral feature observed by Fermi-GBM in GRB 221009A. Detections of H$α$ and Pa$α$ emission from the host galaxy motivate hydrogen recombination seeds, with only indirect support for Ly$α$. A marginal Mg XII feature in the late-time X-ray afterglow provides an event-specific motivation for metal-line seeds, whereas Si XIV, S XVI and iron K-shell transitions are motivated by historical reports of X-ray line features in other gamma-ray bursts. Strong late-time H$_2$ emission detected by the James Webb Space Telescope at the projected burst position motivates our most detailed spectral test. Assuming lateral illumination by the H$_2$ $1-0\,S(1)$ transition at $2.122\,μ{\rm m}$, we calibrate lognormal electron distributions to reproduce the observed MeV photon centroids and widths. We also require IC emission from the ultraviolet (UV) photons driving molecular fluorescence to remain compatible with contemporaneous LAT observations. In a separate test including accompanying molecular transitions, the most favourable configuration, based on the Rh3o photodissociation-region model, approximately describes the MeV feature, although all tested configurations exceed the adopted central spectral references at some energies. For an assumed precursor UV budget, favourable interception substantially reduces the seed-photon energy deficit, but even under ideal excitation and internal escape assumptions, the reference-line photon density in the compact examples falls short of the required value by factors of approximately 4-9. Collisional de-excitation, infrared photon escape and electron cooling impose additional constraints on these configurations. Atomic candidates remain kinematically possible, but their local seed-photon supply is also unestablished.

entry.title: Cosmological Constrained Axion-Portal Inelastic Dark Matter for the LZ Event
entry.summary: The recent high-recoil candidate event reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates dark-matter scenarios with nonstandard kinematics and momentum-dependent interactions. We study a two-state inelastic dark-matter model in which $χ_1$ and $χ_2$ couple off-diagonally to an axion-like particle (ALP) that also couples to gluons and photons. Unlike treatments that assume only one dark-matter state is present today, we track the cosmological evolution of both states. The excited state $χ_2$ is sufficiently long-lived to survive to the present, with its relic fraction determined by the dark-sector conversion process $χ_2χ_2\leftrightarrowχ_1χ_1$. We find that this fraction depends strongly on the Lorentz structure of the DM--ALP interaction. Scalar transition couplings lead to nonperturbative conversion rates with a pronounced resonant structure, yielding a final excited-state fraction that varies nonmonotonically with the mediator mass, from $f_2\sim10^{-4}$ to approximately $1/2$ over the parameter range studied. The relative importance of endothermic and exothermic scattering is therefore parameter dependent. By contrast, pseudoscalar transition couplings preserve $f_2\simeq1/2$, yielding recoil spectra dominated by exothermic $χ_2 N\toχ_1 N$ down-scattering for the benchmarks considered. Benchmark spectra in all four scenarios can peak near the observed recoil energy of $250\,\mathrm{keV}$. Our results demonstrate that the dominant direction of inelastic scattering in direct detection can be dynamically selected by the early-Universe evolution of the dark sector. With additional data, annual modulation measurements could distinguish these scenarios. We further show that the ALP portal can be directly probed at colliders.

entry.title: Multiloop Unitarity from Airy Zeros
entry.summary: Hidden zeros are non-trivial cancellations that make amplitudes or integrands vanish on specific kinematic loci away from propagator poles. They have been shown to uniquely determine tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands in $\Tr(φ^3)$ theory, without assuming factorization. Here we extend both the zeros and the uniqueness results to two, three and four loops at arbitrary multiplicity. We show that two types of zeros naturally enter the all-loop problem. First, tree-level zeros extend to all loop orders and fix relative weights within families of subgraphs attached to vacuum ``loop cores.'' We then show that Kontsevich's matrix Airy function can be used to generate a rich structure of loop level zeros that fix the relative weights of the loop cores themselves. The relative factorization and cut data required by unitarity therefore follow from the combination of tree and Airy loop zeros. These results bring within reach the emergence of unitarity to all orders in perturbation theory.

entry.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
entry.summary: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. The dataset considered represents $10.6$ years of livetime and is three times larger than previous ARA neutrino searches. This search achieves a $28\%$ analysis efficiency for a neutrino flux corresponding to the current experimental upper limits. No neutrino candidates are observed on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. We set a new upper limit on the diffuse UHE neutrino flux, which is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV. We also discuss lessons learned for future searches on large radio arrays.

entry.title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
entry.summary: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Padé resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

entry.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
entry.summary: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_ν\gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. The search found no events on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. The resulting upper limit is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV and provides the first constraints on the flux reported by the KM3NeT Collaboration that are complementary to optical Cherenkov and particle detectors. This limit also constrains UHECR source models, and excludes some models with trans-GZK proton populations at the $90\%$ confidence level. This represents the largest Askaryan detector dataset ever analyzed, demonstrating the feasibility and sensitivity of searches with large detector arrays acting as a single observatory. It also underscores the high acceptance and exposure of Askaryan detector arrays to ultrahigh energy neutrinos.

entry.title: Carrollian bosonic supergravity at order $α'$ and the universal cancellation of higher-curvature divergences
entry.summary: We prove that the Carrollian limit of bosonic supergravity remains finite after including the complete set of four-derivative terms arising from the first $α'$-correction, for an arbitrary Carrollian geometry, i.e., without imposing compatibility conditions on the Carrollian fields. The proof rests on a small set of exact identities satisfied by the leading term of the relativistic Riemann tensor, which is entirely controlled by the intrinsic torsion $K_{μν}=\frac12 \mathcal{L}_τ h_{μν}$ of the Carrollian structure. We explicitly construct the finite action in a manifestly covariant form: the gravitational sector is purely electric, depending only on $K_{μν}$ and on its derivative along $τ^μ$, while the Carrollian curvature and the twist of $τ_μ$ drop out. We then show that higher-curvature contributions obey a universal scaling rule: every scalar built from $N$ relativistic Riemann tensors grows at most as $w^{2N}$ in the Carrollian expansion, so that all purely gravitational $α'^{N-1}$-corrections admit a finite Carrollian limit for arbitrary Carrollian geometries. As applications we show that the $α'^2$- and $α'^3$-corrections of bosonic string theory, including the terms proportional to $ζ(3)$, are finite and non-vanishing in this limit, and that the compatibility conditions $\nabla_μ h_{νρ}=\nabla_μ τ^ν=0$ trivialize the whole gravitational sector.

entry.title: Dynamical obstructions to primary Proca hair and its logarithmic Maxwell continuation
entry.summary: We examine the dynamical admissibility of primary black hole hair in a regularized vector theory of Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The original nontrivial constant norm family cannot satisfy both positive dipole kinetic energy and real nondegenerate radial tensor characteristics. A regular Hamiltonian reduction treats the degenerate boundaries. For asymptotically flat exteriors on the nondegenerate radial branch, adding a Maxwell term for the same vector requires a varying norm. Its positive logarithmic continuation has finite mass at spatial infinity and numerically constructed regular future horizons. The constructed backgrounds satisfy the radial tensor and transverse vector conditions at the sampled points. However, the constrained even angular system has a longitudinal mode with negative squared angular speed. We derive its inverse logarithm coefficient, including both the vector constraint and quartic interaction, and verify it using independent gauge reductions and the full backgrounds. This local angular obstruction persists despite the compatible radial conditions.

entry.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
entry.summary: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

entry.title: Breaking the AGB Color Degeneracy with Variability and H$_2$O: A Consistent Picture of AGB Chemistry, Dust, and the J-Region Across Environments
entry.summary: Resolved asymptotic giant branch (AGB) populations present many observational puzzles. We consider three often treated separately: photometric C/O classification boundaries must be redrawn empirically in new environments; hydrostatic model grids are too blue in bands sampling H2O absorption; and J-region (JAGB) luminosities can differ between fields of a single galaxy. Pulsation connects them into a coherent picture. Using SPHEREx spectroscopy of AGB stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) with JWST/NIRCam photometry and HST time-series of the SN Ia host M101, placed on a common scale by synthetic photometry, we investigate how AGB variability, surface chemistry, and circumstellar dust depend on environment. We develop an F182M index sensitive to 1.9$μ$m H2O absorption that chemically classifies variable AGB stars and reveals oxygen-rich (O-rich) stars degenerate with carbon-rich (C-rich) stars in broadband colors. Because these features arise in extended atmospheric layers, hydrostatic grids struggle to reproduce them. Pulsation and circumstellar dust are asymmetrically linked: nearly all stars with substantial infrared excess are variable, while many variables show little dust. This supports mass loss initiated by pulsation and enhanced by dust formation. Variable O-rich AGB stars in M101 are up to ~0.7 mag redder than their LMC counterparts in dust-sensitive colors, consistent with more efficient silicate-dust production at higher metallicity, while C-rich populations depend less on environment. Color windows that select C-rich stars cleanly in the LMC are therefore 33-68% O-rich in the metal-rich M101. This challenges the J-region's universality as a standard candle while evading standard self-consistency checks. We recommend combining variability, or the infrared excess that implies it, with photometry of molecular features to improve AGB classification at 0.75-5.0$μ$m.

entry.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
entry.summary: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. Until now, however, such constraints have been established only for cold, catalyzed matter. We show that this model-independent bound generalizes to finite temperature along adiabats labelled by the entropy per baryon $\hat{s}$, with the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ assuming the role played by the baryon chemical potential at $T=0$. We find that increasing the temperature shrinks the allowed region monotonically in a form that is universal across structurally distinct mean-field families. For DD2, the density at which the equation of state becomes inconsistent with perturbative QCD decreases from $1.0$ to $0.74\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$ as $\hat{s}$ increases from $0$ to $5$, falling below the central density of the heaviest cold star. By $\hat{s}=4$, seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models are excluded at $6\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$; approximately half of the equations of state drawn from two Bayesian posteriors are excluded by $\hat{s}\simeq3.4$--$4.4$. When mapped onto the QCD phase diagram, the bound becomes active at temperatures of $100$--$150$ MeV, precisely the regime transiently realized in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars.

entry.title: Deflating the Spacetime-Matter Dichotomy
entry.summary: In this paper we analyse scalar-tensor theories-specific instances of which include mainstream inflation and dark energy models-in light of the spacetime-matter dichotomy. We argue that it is difficult to categorise the scalar fields as either a pure aspect of the spacetime structure or a pure form of matter, by focusing on the Jordan vs Einstein frames of these theories. We present and evaluate various interpretational options available, concluding that the spacetime-matter dichotomy becomes untenable in this context. At the same time, the ontological and conceptual category of spacetime can be decoupled from that of gravity, with the latter remaining viable in the context of scalar-tensor theories.

entry.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
entry.summary: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

entry.title: Science Prospects for the Southern Wide-field Gamma-ray Observatory: SWGO
entry.summary: Ground-based gamma-ray astronomy is now well established as a key observational approach to address critical topics at the frontiers of astroparticle physics and high-energy astrophysics. Whilst the field of TeV astronomy was once dominated by arrays of atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes, ground-level particle detection has now been demonstrated to be an equally viable and strongly complementary approach. Ground-level particle detection provides continuous monitoring of the overhead sky, critical for the mapping of extended structures and capturing transient phenomena. As demonstrated by HAWC and LHAASO, the technique provides the best available sensitivity above a few tens of TeV, and for the first time access to the PeV energy range. Despite the success of this approach, there is so far no major ground-level particle-based observatory with access to the Southern sky. HESS, located in Namibia, is the only major gamma-ray instrument in the Southern Hemisphere, and has shown the extraordinary richness of the inner galaxy in the TeV band, but is limited in terms of field of view and energy reach. SWGO is an international effort to construct the first wide-field instrument in the south with deep sensitivity from 100s of GeV into the PeV domain. The project is now close to the end of its development phase and planning for construction of the array in Chile has begun. Here we describe the baseline design, expected sensitivity and resolution, and describe in detail the main scientific topics that will be addressed by this new facility and its initial phase SWGO-A. We show that SWGO will have a transformational impact on a wide range of topics from cosmic-ray acceleration and transport to the nature of dark matter. SWGO represents a key piece of infrastructure for multi-messenger astronomy in the next decade, with strong scientific synergies with the nearby CTA Observatory.

entry.title: Holography for an AdS$_5$ to Hyperscaling-Violating Flow via Dimensional Reduction from 8d Einstein-Matter Gravity
entry.summary: We construct a classical eight-dimensional Einstein--matter model whose reduction on a three-torus admits an AdS$_5$ ultraviolet vacuum and a hyperscaling-violating infrared solution. Neutral scalar winding maintains the ultraviolet vacuum, while its disappearance allows the infrared geometry to become locally AdS$_8$. The same reduction fixes the running gauge coupling, charged scalar mass and interactions. We derive the vacuum conditions, the radial evolution equations and the infrared spectrum. Scalar and vector superfluid orders are then compared using exact ultraviolet zero modes and analytic infrared eigenvalue identities. The scalar and vector instabilities in the infrared coincide at a unique scalar mass above the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound. Their nonlinear competition is governed by a quartic free energy that includes electric response and the change between fixed chemical potential and fixed density. For the interpolating geometry, we identify the conditions under which the two orders can appear together and form a locally stable phase.

entry.title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
entry.summary: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.
